items.title: Jasper Taylor Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: Baby Dodds was known for the press. And, uh, it, it was really a press. And it was musical and I don't know. The nearest man to the press roll, uh, to Baby Dodds was, uh, Sudie.

ctx.x: Of other New Orleans, uh, drummers, do you remember any, uh, others you mentioned, Cottrell, who first came up. Do you remember any of the other bands that came up like when Joe Oliver's band first came up?

Oh, yeah. I know about Jimmy Nooney, when he first came up. And, uh, I think he was with the Joe Oliver band for a while. And then he had a band of his own very shortly after that. And then, uh, I had some wonderful drummers. Uh, Baby Hall was, uh, New Orleans drummer. And he had, he's one that had a great reputation for holding the time very steady. Uh, if he knocked off at a certain tempo, the beginning of that tempo was the same at the ending of the piece as it was in the beginning. Uh, and he, the…

I know Baby was famous for that press roll. I used to ask him to try to explain it a little, how he did it. And he, he would never, he could show you, but he wouldn't put it in words. Can you tell a little bit? What do you do? Just sort of drag your stick across the drum?
